To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chronic graft-versus host disease is associated with significant impairment of quality of life, as assessed by two validated instruments, the SF-36 (a measure of general health) and the FACT-BMT (a measure of transplant specific health).

the NIH chronic graft-versus- host disease (cGVHD) severity score, which includes the extent and severity of organ involvement and functional status, is associated with quality of life as measured by the Medical Outcomes Study Short Form-36 and Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-BMT instruments in patients with chronic GVHD.
chronic GVHD is a systemic disease that causes a broad range of symptoms, including physical, social and emotional problems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of chronic GVHD on quality of life (QoL) of patients with chronic GVHD.
the development, implementation and validation of a new patient reported outcomes (PRO) instrument for use in clinical trials in the field of hematopoietic stem cell transplant.
the development, validation and use of the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Bone Marrow Transplantation (FACT-BMT) questionnaire.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NIH cGVHD severity criteria are useful for predicting the impact of chronic GVHD on QOL.
the QOL of cGVHD patients is worse than that of healthy controls and is comparable to that of other chronic conditions, and that the NIH criteria for cGVHD severity are associated with QOL.
chronic GVHD is associated with a compromised quality of life.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NIH criteria for chronic GVHD severity are associated with compromised QOL, and may be used as a functional outcome for clinical studies.
NIH criteria are a useful and practical way to define chronic GVHD severity, which is associated with compromised QOL.
chronic GVHD is associated with a significant compromise in quality of life, and that this compromise is independent of the age of the patient and the severity of the disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chronic GVHD is associated with significant QOL impairment in a variety of domains, and that the SF-36 is a useful tool to assess this in clinical trials and practice.
chronic GVHD is associated with significant impairment in QOL.
cGVHD is a chronic, debilitating disease that affects patients’ QOL.
